_about: (5b-1: `other_routes` — a signed START, posted to /agents/{agent}/desktop-start where the agent comes from the URL so the payload's agent_member_id is the press's agent, and a signed CLOCK press of one agent or of a computer's setup, posted to /desktop/setups/{sid}/clock, ride the road too, their rows with session_key null; `never_direct_other`: the press of the WHOLE computer and an edit never ride it.) How a press becomes the ROW the same-network direct road sends (story 4993 · web PR 5a). The web builds the row from the very body it would post to the server; the server builds the Mac's payload for the same press from the same body — so the two must agree, and this ONE file is what the web's test (apps/web/src/lib/phone-direct.test.ts) and the server's test (backend/tests/test_4993_direct_rows_realdb.py) both read. A plain (non-sealed) instruction never rides the direct road. The row's command_id is the press's idempotency key; its created_at is the phone's clock.
